bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Elongated client decision cycles for AI projects; BFSI sector contraction pressures; Domestic channel policy changes by OEMs (Microsoft); Sustainability of TMT upturn.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; disciplined execution; focused on continuity during leadership transition; confident in AI pipeline conversion despite macro headwinds.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: AI-led orders now 18% of total book indicating rapid product mix shift; Domestic business already recovered most of the OEM direct-billing loss within 4 quarters despite reported degrowth; 90% of workforce already AI-certified creating a latent margin lever if utilization dips.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 'Declared interim dividend of 125% per share' (deck's own wording, stated alongside the Q1FY27 financial highlights).
- Consolidated balance-sheet position at Q1'27: 'Gross Cash and Cash Equivalent' 567.0 INR crs and 'Cash & net cash position' 67.0 INR crs - the latter having moved from -62.5 in Q1'26 and -280.0 in Q2'26 to 30.7 in Q4'26.
- Working capital in the domestic arm loosened sharply - 'Net working capital/GC' at 0.87 in Q1'27 versus 0.48 in Q4'26 and 0.45 in Q2'26/Q3'26, with domestic DSO at 65 days versus 47 in Q4'26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Proprietary Platformation™ framework underpinning its AI-first Modernization Engineering positioning
- Deep hyperscaler partnerships — Microsoft, AWS, Salesforce and Snowflake — used to deliver AI solutions to clients
- Microsoft standing: continuing member of the Microsoft Inner Circle and Partner AI Council, among the first companies recognised as a Microsoft Frontier Partner, and an Official Microsoft Fabric Featured Partner
- AWS standing: AWS Premier Tier Services Partner (highest level of recognition in the AWS Partner Network) and AWS Gen AI Competency Partner
- Owned Agentic AI platform AgentBridge, launched in FY26 and already running production-grade agents for the Company's own HR and Finance teams
- Research partnerships with IISc (India) and the Wharton School (US) on Agentic AI research and innovation
- AI-trained workforce — more than 92% of the workforce and 80% of managers trained in AI via Sonata University, with Vibe Code training rolled out organisation-wide
- Sticky client base with an aggregated Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) score of 4.3 out of 5 and 23 new customers added during the Financial Year
- Recognised employer brand (Jombay WOW Workplace 2025 in IT and ITES, Team Marksmen Most Preferred Workplace 2025-26, ET Now Best Organizations to Work 2025) supporting talent retention
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Human capital development, retention and labour practices — Flagged as a material risk in the BRSR: Sonata is a people-centric organisation and its sustained success is closely tied to its ability to attract, engage and retain highly skilled technology professionals; as the global shift toward digital transformation intensifies, the growing imbalance in skilled talent has become increasingly evident. Mitigation runs through engagement initiatives, the DNA (Deep Nurtured Attributes) core values and a rewards and recognition framework.
- Privacy protection and cybersecurity / data breach exposure — Flagged as a material risk in the BRSR: the expansion of operations along with increased adoption of remote working models may elevate the risk of data breaches; any failure to ensure data privacy or to report incidents in a timely manner could result in legal penalties, reputational damage with clients and potential financial exposure. Mitigated by certification audits for the Information Security Management Framework aligned with ISO 27001 and the Service Management Framework aligned with ISO 20000, plus security investments, access controls, threat monitoring and employee awareness training.
- Climate change — climate risk, GHG emissions and possible carbon taxation — Flagged as a material risk and opportunity in the BRSR: climate-related risks are increasingly impacting the operational environment and financial performance, and possible implementation of carbon taxation in the near term could influence the growth trajectory; transitioning to a low-carbon economy may require substantial upfront investment.
- Corporate governance and business ethics / regulatory compliance burden — Flagged as a material risk and opportunity in the BRSR: full legal compliance must be maintained and internal practices constantly updated to stay ahead of changing regulations; implementing high governance standards requires significant resources, described as a negative but mitigated financial impact and a vital investment for maintaining stakeholder confidence.
- Dependence on the pace of client digital-transformation adoption — Customer relationships are central to Sonata's business strategy and the growth of the customer base is closely aligned with the rate at which organisations adopt digital transformation initiatives — making revenue growth a function of external enterprise IT spending cycles.
- Geographic revenue concentration in North America — The North America business now represents over 74% of total revenue, up from approximately 54% three years ago, so demand or client conditions in a single market drive the bulk of the business; exports contribute 39% of the entity's total turnover.
- Single-activity / single-service-line concentration — The BRSR reports one business activity — Information Technology Services and Solutions (IT consultancy, computer programming, modernization, testing support) — at more than 90% of turnover, with computer programming, consultancy and related activities at 100% of turnover, leaving no diversification outside IT services.
- Execution risk on the AI-led pivot — Growth is concentrated in a set of explicit bets — AI-enabled services scaling to a stated share of revenue, large-deal pursuits, and the HLS and BFSI invest verticals — which depend on continued AI adoption by clients and on sustaining hyperscaler partner status (Microsoft Inner Circle/Frontier/Fabric, AWS Premier Tier and Gen AI Competency) rather than on a diversified base.

business.body:
- Stated positioning is a three-part construct: 'Outcome-led Business Transformation', 'AI-first Technology Platforms' and 'AI-native Service Delivery', summarised as 'Engineering the AI enterprise'.
- Named capabilities under that umbrella: 'Domain-driven customer-enabling operations', 'Legacy Modernization', 'AI-ready data', 'Resilient AI command center', 'AI-powered engineering' and 'Autonomous ops'.
- Go-to-market is 'Micro vertical focused' across BFS, HLS, RMD and 'Tech and emerging'; the deck's four vertical labels are TMT (Technology, Media and Telecom), BFSI, HLS (Healthcare and Life Sciences) and RMD (Retail, Manuf., Travel and Distribution).
- The Microsoft relationship is presented as the core moat: 'Microsoft-Sonata 360 Degree Partnership: 30+ Years', with '3500+ Team On Microsoft Technologies', 'Annual $650M+ MSFT Annual Revenue Tied to the Microsoft Stack', '400+ Clients Across The Globe', Azure Expert MSP status, '10 Advanced Specialization in Dynamics 365, Data Analytics, Teams, CAF, M365, Azure' and 'Microsoft AI Council Partner Member'.
- Ecosystem is stated as broader than Microsoft: '360 ecosystem partnerships - Microsoft, AWS, Snowflake, Servicenow'.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Two-business structure] The deck reports International Services and Domestic Business separately with radically different economics - the Domestic Business (SITL) shows Q1'27 revenue of 2505.6 INR crs against Gross Contribution of just 78.5 INR crs and EBITDA (Before Forex & OI) margin of 2.4%, consistent with its 'Grow Core Reselling/Platform' description; International Services shows Q1'27 revenue of 777.2 INR crs on a 15.4% EBITDA (Before Forex & OI) margin. Gross revenue of the reselling arm is not comparable to services revenue.
- [Client concentration] Revenue from Top 10 clients fell to 51.0% in Q1'27 from 54.0% in Q4'26 and 56% in Q1'26; Top 20 was 70.0% versus 69.0% in Q4'26. New customers added: 7 in Q1'27, same as Q4'26 and Q1'26.
- [Client-size cohorts] $5+ Mn clients numbered 12 in Q1'27 (13 in Q1'26), $3-5 Mn 9 (6), $1-3 Mn 32 (39) - the small-account cohort has been shrinking through the five quarters shown.
- [Geography mix] International Services revenue by geography at Q1'27: USA 71%, Europe 23%, ROW 6% - Europe has risen from 16.0% in Q1'26 while ROW fell from 10.0%.
- [Disclosure change] The covering letter describes the file as a 'revised Investors' Presentation for the quarter ended 30th June, 2026', i.e. a restatement of an earlier submission; the deck does not say what was revised.

business.body: Sonata Software Limited (“SSL”) is primarily engaged in providing Information Technology Services and Solutions — IT consultancy, computer programming, modernization and testing support related activities — to customers in the United States of America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, Australia and India. The Company describes itself as operating in two spheres: International IT Services and a Domestic products-and-services business run through its India arm Sonata Information Technology Limited (SITL), which expands the Microsoft channel, partners with other ISVs and pursues large System Integration deals. It is a public limited company incorporated and domiciled in India, with its registered office at Mumbai and operational headquarters at Bengaluru, and is listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited.

outlook.body: $95M total (Q4); AI-led portion $16.9M (Q4) / $49M (FY26), representing 18% of total book. Large deals: 2 won in Q4, 8 in FY26.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: $280M AI-led pipeline across 100+ clients; Harmoni.AI and AgentBridge differentiated offerings; Expansion in BFSI payments modernization and TMT upturn.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Position Sonata as an AI-first Modernization Engineering company that helps enterprises transform from legacy systems to intelligent business platforms
- Embed AI across the organisation — client solutions, delivery and internal functions — and convert innovation into measurable business impact, shaping the path toward 'Sonata.AI'
- Drive platform-led transformation (Platformation.AI), agentic AI operating models and partner-led GTM acceleration (PLF-driven), moving clients from tool-based adoption to autonomous AI-driven execution at scale
- Build and scale proprietary AI platforms — Harmoni.AI, IntelliQA and AgentBridge — as the delivery vehicle for AI-led offerings
- Deepen hyperscaler collaborations with Microsoft (Inner Circle, Partner AI Council, Frontier Partner, Fabric Featured Partner) and AWS (Premier Tier Services Partner, Gen AI Competency Partner)
- Scale the Invest Verticals — Healthcare & Life Sciences (HLS) and Banking, Financial Services & Insurance (BFSI) — through sharper verticalization
- Grow the India business (SITL) on three pillars: expand the Microsoft channel with sharper focus on the SMC segment including incubation of the new Sonata-on-Cloud (SoC) offering; broaden partnerships with other ISVs beyond the three hyperscale CSPs; and win large System Integration (SI) deals
- Structurally strengthen operations through technology-driven optimization, including Program Edge automation of internal workflows with an AI layer
- Build AI capability in the workforce through Sonata University so employees can partner with clients on their AI journeys
- Forge academic and research collaborations (Wharton, IISc) to build an ecosystem around AI and emerging technologies
- Operate responsibly against the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) charter while delivering sustainable growth
- The Company follows a stated practice of rewarding members based on performance and future outlook, and dividends paid and recommended are in accordance with its Dividend Distribution Policy adopted under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations (available on the Company's website). For FY 2025-26 this took the form of three interim dividends declared and paid during the year plus a final dividend recommended by the Board, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM, with the final dividend payable on or after 10th August, 2026 to shareholders on the register as on 17th July, 2026. No amounts were transferred to reserves for the Financial Year ended 31st March, 2026, and there was no change in the paid-up share capital during the year. Governance intent is framed as enhancement of long-term shareholder value while protecting the interests of other stakeholders without compromising on compliance, with the roles of Chairperson and Managing Director & CEO separated for a balanced governance structure.
- Committed to transitioning to renewable energy sources and achieving carbon neutrality by 2030, thereby decreasing reliance on grid-based energy
- Implemented a comprehensive set of initiatives to enhance energy efficiency and reduce emissions across operations, which the Company says have produced measurable reductions in operating costs and lowered its overall carbon footprint
- Successful completion of certification audits for the Information Security Management Framework aligned with ISO 27001 and the Service Management Framework aligned with ISO 20000
- Diversity and inclusion: gender and cultural diversity maintained at 31% across the workforce; women comprise 31% of permanent employees and 30% of total employees, and 14.29% of the Board of Directors
- Inclusion programme build-out — launch of the Women Mentoring Program, the Allyship Award, expansion of SWAN (Sonata Women Advocacy Network) across regions, and extended medical insurance coverage for LGBTQ colleagues
- Workforce AI capability building through Sonata University, with more than 92% of the workforce and 80% of managers trained in AI
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013
- Grievance redressal for external stakeholders through the Third-Party Code of Conduct and Business Ethics together with the Vigil Mechanism Policy; no complaints filed by communities, investors, employees and workers, customers or value-chain partners in FY 2026, and all shareholder complaints were promptly resolved
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed text discloses no plant, capacity or physical capex programme — Sonata's expansion is asset-light and platform/capability-led. In FY26 the Company launched AgentBridge, its cloud-agnostic Agentic AI platform for building and deploying next-generation Agentic AI solutions, and operationalized it internally with production-grade agents running for the HR and Finance teams. Capability build-out continued through Sonata University, which trained more than 92% of the workforce and 80% of managers in AI and delivered organisation-wide Vibe Code training, and through Program Edge, under which internal workflows — including immigration management and compensation and benefits administration — are being automated with an AI layer on top. Ecosystem expansion took the form of research partnerships with IISc (India) and the Wharton School (US) on Agentic AI, and of deeper hyperscaler alliances: Microsoft (continuing Inner Circle and Partner AI Council member, among the first recognised as a Microsoft Frontier Partner, Official Microsoft Fabric Featured Partner) and AWS (Premier Tier Services Partner, Gen AI Competency Partner), alongside Salesforce and Snowflake. Market expansion is being pursued by scaling the invest verticals HLS and BFSI, by deepening the North America business, and in India (SITL) by expanding the Microsoft channel into the SMC segment, broadening ISV partnerships beyond the three hyperscaler CSPs, and winning large System Integration deals that integrate Cisco, IBM, Dell and other ISV infrastructures with leading cloud platforms. The workforce stood at 6200+ Sonatians.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- AI is moving from experimentation to industrial-scale adoption, and is becoming the operating layer of the modern enterprise rather than just a capability
- Enterprises are shifting from using technology as a tool for cost efficiency to viewing it as a core engine for commercial reinvention, moving beyond simple task automation toward augmented intelligence that creates new business models and revenue streams
- Organizations are moving beyond fragmented pilots to embedding AI across revenue, operations and engineering
- AI-led opportunities are scaling in the pipeline and are being pursued across 100+ clients, monetised through operational efficiency gains, faster time to market/customer experience, and transformation of business models
- FY26 was a year of resilience as the Company navigated headwinds from the market and from a few key clients; operations were strengthened structurally through technology-driven optimization, which management says reflected in growth and profit expansion
- Management intends to leverage Sonata's size and scale to deliver 'enterprise velocity' and position the Company as a compelling choice for clients, via differentiated capabilities, partnerships and sharper verticalization
- Client demand evidenced in delivered use cases — engineering productivity and build-cycle gains, ITSM cost reduction and automation-led transaction reduction at named client types (education services, travel & tourism, financial services)
- AI now accounts for 18% of the order book
- AI-led opportunities have scaled to represent 30% of the pipeline, highlighting strong adoption momentum
- AI opportunities are being actively pursued across 100+ clients
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Sonata delivered resilient Q4FY26 with 20.2% EBITDA margins driven by AI-enabled utilization (91.8%) despite flat international revenue, while domestic business stabilized post-OEM direct-billing shock. The appointment of Rajsekhar Datta Roy (30-year veteran/AI-architect) as CEO signals an aggressive pivot to monetize the $280M AI pipeline, targeting BFSI and TMT recovery in FY27.

open.item: AI-enabled Services are expected to contribute 20% of the Company's revenue by the end of FY27.
The investment verticals Healthcare & Life Sciences (HLS) and Banking, Financial Services & Insurance (BFSI) are stated to be on track to scale to $250M in revenue over the next 3 to 5 years.

The India business (SITL) will be grown on three strategic pillars — expanding the Microsoft channel with sharper focus on the SMC segment including incubation of the new Sonata-on-Cloud (SoC) offering, broadening partnerships with other ISVs beyond the three hyperscale CSPs, and winning large System Integration deals.
